cell_type.evidence: To unravel the molecular machinery, we performed immunoprecipitation mass spectrometry (IP-MS) of DLX2-Flag in ectomesenchymal progenitors, revealing LAP2α as a critical interactor.

developmental_stage.evidence: inferred: The ectomesenchyme generates much of the craniofacial skeleton, sutures, and diverse connective tissues in the mammalian head, yet its derivation from embryonic stem cells (ESCs) and the underlying molecular drivers remain poorly defined.

disease_state.evidence: inferred: Here, we identified Dlx2 as a key regulator that efficiently directed murine ESCs towards Msx1+ ectomesenchyme, recapitulating the developmental trajectory.

material_type.evidence: inferred: These Msx1+ progenitors expressed classical craniofacial markers and retained robust osteochondral bipotency in vitro and in vivo.
